//: EAS build and submit profiles for PartyBooth.
Build numbers are NOT in app.config.ts. `cli.appVersionSource: remote` puts the
counter on EAS and `autoIncrement` bumps it per store build, because App Store
Connect refuses a build number it has already seen and says so only AFTER the
upload — a number kept in a file two people can edit is a rejected submission on
the day it matters. `eas build:version:get` reads the current values.
Every value under `submit` that identifies an account is read from the environment
rather than committed. An App Store Connect app id and an Apple team id are not
secrets, but they are per-owner, and this repo has to clone and build with an empty
environment.
Step-by-step: docs/store/ios-submission.md and docs/store/android-internal.md.
Android internal testing — the path to guests' phones on 5 Aug, because a new
Play account cannot reach production for 14 days (PLAN.md). Internal testing
has no review queue, so the opt-in link works within minutes of the upload.
releaseStatus draft is deliberate: the upload lands, you look at it, and you
roll it out. On internal testing that costs one click and buys the chance to
notice a wrong version code before testers get it.
iOS here is TestFlight — the fallback if the store build is still in review on
the 5th.
ascAppId is the NUMERIC App Store Connect app id (App Information → General →
Apple ID), not the bundle identifier. Confusing those two is the most common
`eas submit` failure and the error does not say which one it wanted.
Set APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD to run non-interactively; without it the CLI
prompts, which is fine locally and hangs in CI.
